question: The European Disability Rights Week presents an important opportunity to highlight the challenges faced by persons with disabilities across the EU and the action required for their full inclusion in society. A critical issue that remains unresolved and continues to limit the ability of persons with disabilities to participate equally in society is their unimpeded access to all means of transport.

In the European Parliament’s Committee on Transport and Tourism, we pay particular attention to the concerns expressed by many of our fellow citizens about accessibility problems in public transport and we aim to step up the protection of the rights of passengers with reduced mobility.

The implementation of stricter standards to facilitate accessibility and the development of innovative transport solutions are essential to promote social integration and equality in an inclusive society. In this context and on the occasion of the International Day of Persons with Disabilities: 1.
What further initiatives will the Commission take to fund investment to improve the accessibility of public transport and all means of transport for people with reduced mobility?
What steps will the Commission take to ensure the development of improved infrastructure and the implementation of existing European legislation to promote inclusivity in the transport sector?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.2.2025) In the current multiannual financial framework 2021-2027, different funding instruments, notably the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) and Cohesion Policy Funds can be used to support barrier-free access to transport.

CEF finances actions to improve transport infrastructure accessibility, and to date has included a particular focus on accessibility for persons with reduced mobility in railway stations1. The Social Climate Fund was established to support vulnerable groups, among others, in the fair transition to clean mobility.

Provided that the conditions of Regulation (EU) 2023/9552 are respected, a part of this money could be used by Member States to improve the access of persons with disabilities and persons with reduced mobility to sustainable transport solutions, including making public transport infrastructure more accessible.

The revised guidelines for the development of the trans-European network (TEN-T)3 require that, when developing the TEN-T infrastructure, priority should be given, among others, to measures improving accessibility for all users, including persons with disabilities or reduced mobility.

This should be pursued in particular by means of better integration of the different transport modes into the urban nodes, including by developing multimodal passenger hubs, which should facilitate seamless connections of TEN-T to public transport infrastructure by 2030.

The European Union has adopted a wide range of legislation to bring about improvements in access to transport for persons with disabilities and persons with reduced mobility4. The President of the Commission has indicated in her political guidelines5 the new Commission’s commitment to implement and enforce EU legislation in this area.
1 Since 2014, nearly 150 CEF projects included such measures. 2 Regulation (EU) 2023/955 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023 establishing a Social
